profiles.title: The Savior Not Made by Hands
profiles.subject: Christ

overview.text: The Savior Not Made by Hands is associated with the Holy Mandylion, the cloth bearing Christ’s face in the Church’s account of Abgar of Edessa. The OCA commemorates its translation to Constantinople on August 16.
overview.reason: Necessary concise account of a modern published source; substantial verbatim reproduction is not licensed. This is an editorial summary, not the source author’s wording.

blocks.text: The example is Simon Ushakov’s historical depiction of Christ’s face upon a suspended cloth. It represents the received Mandylion subject; the painted panel itself is an artist’s work, not the cloth described in the traditional account.

blocks.text: The OCA relates that the ill ruler Abgar sought Christ’s help and that Christ imprinted his face on a cloth sent to Edessa. The same account dates the transfer to Constantinople to 944. These are identified as the published Church narrative and its dated commemoration.

blocks.text: Metropolitan Tikhon explains the feast on two levels: the particular Mandylion and Christ himself as the true Image of the Father who freely became human.

blocks.text: Who is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of every creature: For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him: And he is before all things, and by him all things consist.
